done_when: Forge's own CI splits its test groups by recorded test time (a committed .test_durations file that pytest-split reads, with a plain way to refresh it), so no group of the last run takes more than 70% of its time limit; this is Forge's own CI only, so new and existing client repos get nothing

findings.body: The required performance check remains unfinished. The latest handoff commit, ab01ef7a, explicitly states that wall times including setup are still missing for the corrected three/six/eight matrix. The measured older matrix exceeded the target on Ubuntu group 2 (459 seconds) and macOS group 1 (436 seconds). The successful local close run and collection estimates do not establish platform job wall times. Complete the corrected matrix run and verify every Ubuntu/macOS group finishes within 420 seconds and every Windows group within 840 seconds. The coordinator's rulings retain the current group counts pending measurements; this finding requires the outstanding check, not another speculative count increase.

why: Forge's CI splits tests into groups by count with no recorded test times, so the first macOS and Windows groups keep hitting their time limits and cancelled jobs send items back to workers
